title: How to "Dry Age" a Steak in Two Hours | Techniquely with Lan Lam
summary: Lan Lam presents a home method to emulate dry-aged beef flavors in a matter of hours using shiokoji (koji) as a fermentation-inspired marinade on flank steak. The video opens with an overview of why dry-aged beef is prized—tenderness and intensified flavor with pronounced umami—then explains the enzymatic changes that occur during traditional aging. It introduces koji-based shiokoji and its enzymes (proteases, amylases, lipases), demonstrates selecting and preparing a steak (notably flank with silver skin removed), and shows coating the meat with shiokoji and refrigerating for 2–24 hours. After aging, the steak is cooked with a reverse-sear: a 300°F oven finish to about 130–135°F, followed by a quick skillet sear. The serving ideas include shiokoji compound butter, lemon, and flake salt. The video also touches on flavor variations and practical considerations for home cooks, including cost and practicality in lieu of traditional dry-aging.

sections.title: Home practicality of dry-aging
